summary:
Section 1 designates the Act as the “Dr. Emmanuel Bilirakis and Honorable Jennifer Wexton National Plan to End Parkinson’s Act.” Section 2 amends title III of the Public Health Service Act, 42 U.S.C. 241 et seq., by adding a new part W, “Parkinson’s and Related Disorders,” consisting of new PHSA § 399OO, codified at 42 U.S.C. 280n.

New § 399OO establishes a mandatory Department of Health and Human Services initiative, the “National Parkinson’s Project,” under which the Secretary of Health and Human Services must carry out a national project to prevent, diagnose, treat, and cure “Parkinson’s,” defined to include Parkinson’s disease and all other neurodegenerative Parkinsonisms, including multiple system atrophy, corticobasal degeneration, progressive supranuclear palsy, and Parkinson’s-related dementia. The Project’s required activities include creating, maintaining, and periodically updating an integrated national plan; conducting an annual assessment; estimating current Federal investment and, if applicable, necessary investment; coordinating Parkinson’s-related research and services across Federal agencies; encouraging development of safe and effective treatments, strategies, and other approaches; improving early diagnosis and coordination of care; reviewing impacts on individuals with Parkinson’s and caregivers and families; coordinating with international bodies to the extent possible; and, to the extent practicable, collaborating to avoid duplication of research for related disorders.

Under § 399OO(d), not later than 24 months after enactment and annually thereafter, the Secretary must assess national progress in preparing for and responding to the escalating burden of Parkinson’s, including priority-action recommendations, planned or completed implementation steps, whether recommendations can be implemented under existing law, and other items the Secretary determines appropriate.

Section 399OO(e) requires the Secretary to establish and maintain an Advisory Council on Parkinson’s Research, Care, and Services. The Council must include specified Federal representatives from listed agencies and 10 non-Federal expert members representing specified patient, caregiver, clinical, research, and nonprofit categories, including representation of minority, disproportionately affected, and underrepresented communities. The Council must meet quarterly for two years after establishment and thereafter at the Secretary’s discretion; convene an annual Parkinson’s research meeting beginning not later than 24 months after enactment; and hold such meetings publicly. Beginning not later than 18 months after enactment and annually thereafter, it must report to the Secretary and Congress on federally funded efforts, recommendations, priority actions, evaluation of national-plan implementation, and implementation steps. The Council terminates at the end of calendar year 2035.

Section 399OO(f) requires Federal departments and agencies possessing Parkinson’s-related information to share it with the Secretary, consistent with applicable disclosure obligations, as necessary for the Council’s report. Section 399OO(g) sunsets § 399OO at the end of calendar year 2035. The Act contains no express authorization of appropriations or direct appropriation.
